discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae: radioactively powered transients from neutron-star mergers that establish them as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis

nominees.name: Ryan J. Foley
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

subfield: Astrophysics: multi-messenger transients and nuclear astrophysics
motivation: Metzger and collaborators predicted in 2010 that the neutron-rich ejecta of neutron-star mergers would power a distinctive thermal transient through the radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei. Kasen showed with radiative-transfer calculations that lanthanide opacities make this 'kilonova' red, faint and short-lived, which set out what observers should look for. On 17 August 2017, Foley's Swope team made the first optical detection of the counterpart to GW170817. The kilonova that followed matched the predictions closely: fast blue emission, then red, lanthanide-rich emission. This linked gravitational waves to the electromagnetic universe and identified a major origin of the heaviest elements, such as gold and platinum. The discovery turned a fleeting gravitational-wave signal into a physical understanding of nuclear matter, element formation and cosmic expansion. It is a key case of theory and fast observation working together, and it opened multi-messenger astronomy.
